The chart's decompose stage will split the WORK; that is a different act from spawning child NODES, and if decompose finds a seam that genuinely proves apart, a child is cast then.

questions.a: THE .pyc HEADER ANSWERS A REAL QUESTION THAT IS NOT THE ONE BEING ASKED. It records when the file was last compiled BY ANYBODY. The loop needs to know when the file was last compiled BY ITSELF. Every term in the comparison — source mtime, embedded mtime — is readable by every process and identical for all of them, so the predicate cannot in principle distinguish two processes of different ages over one tree. It is not a bug in the arithmetic; the evidence does not contain the asker.

AND THE SECOND ACTOR THAT DEFEATS IT IS THIS SYSTEM'S NORMAL OPERATION, NOT AN EDGE CASE. CC runs proofs, doors and probes in the very tree the daemon watches, every few minutes. Any one of those runs refreshes the header. So the guard's reliability is inversely proportional to how much work is being done — it is at its blindest exactly when the code is moving fastest, which is when it is needed.

THE QUIET FACE, NAMED HERE FOR THE FIRST TIME: probe modules are exec'd fresh off their path each pass, so a probe BODY is always current, but its `from cairn... import` statements resolve through the boot-time sys.modules. Reproduced deterministically 2026-08-18: a fresh-exec'd module read 'boot' from a dependency whose disk source said 'edited', and importlib.invalidate_caches() changed nothing. Every probe in the system may be evaluating its trigger against code that no longer exists, with every surface reporting healthy.

THE INSTRUMENT CAUGHT THE PATIENT'S ILLNESS, and it was found by aiming the finished probe at the world rather than by reasoning. loop_not_stale took its second reading — 'does this folder import cleanly right now?' — with discover() IN THIS PROCESS, and this process is the ground loop, the suspect. Measured 2026-08-18 in a throwaway tree: a process holding a pre-edit module reads the probe folder as ONE ImportError while a fresh interpreter over the same disk reads ZERO. So the in-process reading agrees with the bench exactly when the bench is wrong, and the probe's signature could only ever read TRUE when run from somewhere other than the loop it watches — which is why the smoke fire showed would_trigger:true and the live loop stayed silent. Fixed by taking the reading in a child process seeded from this one's sys.path (loop_not_stale.fresh_import_reading), which is also what this ticket's falsifier declared in words on the day it was cast. A refusal from that child is returned as a refusal and never read as clean.

THE DEPOSIT IS DURABLE AND UNDELIVERABLE, measured rather than assumed, and it is not this ticket's to fix. The probe fired in the LIVE loop at 2026-08-18T04:24:37Z and its carry is in the bus transit table (bus_traffic, sender ground_loop) naming benched_but_importing: ['survey']. It never arrives: the bus's own diagnostics carry 258 'undelivered' rows, every one of them 'harbor_master was discovered by its probes/ folder, not registered with a device — it is on the roster to be PULSED, not to be paged.' So the watch accumulates in a record of truth that has no reader, and the trouble it would have caused a human to look at — ground-loop-device-survey — is still OPEN with count frozen at 1 since 2026-08-18T03:44:07Z, first_seen == last_seen, the self-sealing freeze this whole node is about. RECORDED, NOT BUILT: giving harbor_master a registered device is another component's voyage and outside this ticket's bounds.

THE QUIET FACE, CAUGHT IN A LIVE RECORD ON THE DAY IT WAS DESCRIBED. That same 04:24:37Z deposit carries the probe's NEW fields (also_watches, reproduces_here_but_not_fresh, fresh_reading_refused) and carries coverage: null. Both at once is the quiet face itself: the ProbeCache re-exec'd the edited probe body off disk (identity is path+mtime), and that fresh body then bound 'from cairn... import staleness' through the boot-time sys.modules, so it called a staleness that predates the rewrite and has no coverage tally to give. Loop started 00:50:39Z; staleness.py was written 04:18:01Z. New code and old dependency in one artifact, and every surface reported healthy.

THREE OF THE EIGHT ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA NAMED AN INSTRUMENT THAT COULD NOT HAVE SHOWN WHAT IT CLAIMED, and each was replaced at the verdict rather than reported around. (2) a text grep of staleness.py for 'mtime'/'ImportError' returns 16 and 5 — from the module's own PROSE explaining which face a difference corresponds to, and from the retired header comparison deliberately kept as reported-but-not-deciding payload. A grep cannot tell an explanation from a special case; the instrument that works AST-walks the six deciding functions and asserts the banned spellings are not among the identifiers they touch or the constants they compare against. (4) reverting the predicate to HEAD leaves test_discovery.py GREEN, because its prove-apart pair INJECTS the staleness answer instead of reading the real one — the deciding branch in loop.py had to be mutated instead (if False: 4 red; if True: 8 red; disjoint sets). (1) `git stash` cannot make the HEAD-red tooth FAIL rather than ERROR, because HEAD has no read_all at all; a worktree plus a shim supplying that NAME and nothing else is what made 'fails by name' checkable. THE POINT THAT GENERALISES: an acceptance criterion is only as real as its instrument, and a criterion measured by an instrument that cannot bite is a hollow green — which Law 8 rates worse than a red, because a red is distrusted by construction and a false green gets leaned on.

24% OF HELD OBJECTS READ UNDECIDABLE, against a hypothesis that predicted 'a small, enumerable set'. Measured 2026-08-18 in a process that first imported every importable module under cairn/ (170 succeeded): modules_read 172, comparable_objects 1133, undecidable_objects 364, findings 0, modules wholly undecidable 0. The falsifier as written ('more than a handful of MODULES wholly undecidable') never came close to firing, and the charter's red does not fire either — UNDECIDABLE never reads CURRENT. What the miss costs is REACH, not correctness, and the honest form of it is the number being printed in the coverage tally rather than the adjective being kept in the prose. This is also why read_all returns (findings, tally): findings alone cannot separate 'compared 1133 objects, none disagreed' from 'could compare nothing', and those read identically at every surface.

THE TROUBLE DID NOT CLOSE, AND THE RECORD SAYS SO RATHER THAN LETTING IT LOOK SELF-CLEARING. ground-loop-device-survey is still OPEN at the close: count 1, first_seen == last_seen == 2026-08-18T03:44:07.111351+00:00, cleared_by []. A fixed predicate structurally cannot reach an already-benched device — discovery.discover() is called with skip=set(self._benched) and those folders 'are not even opened this pass' (discovery.py:177/187), while loop.py:380 rebuilds the bench from trouble.live() every pass — so the only exit is TroubleDevice.clear(), and the process holding the wrong reading is the one that has to be replaced. It waits on a restart of pid 973171, which is Akien's to perform. This build changes the NEXT misattribution, not this one.
